svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.2.1.1 Defined Words
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.2 DEFINITIONS

g.text: between the roof and the ceiling
first storey floor, basement not counted
top of floor to top of floor above,
or to the ceiling at the top
floor 2 m (6′-6¾″) or less above grade:

svg.text: Words in italics are defined in Article 1.4.1.2. of Division
“the lowest of the average levels of finished ground adjoining
each exterior wall of a building, except that localized
depressions need not be considered in the determination of
“the uppermost storey having its floor level not more than 2 m
“a storey or storeys of a building located below the first
“that portion of a building that is situated between the top of
any floor and the top of the floor next above it, and if there
is no floor above it, that portion between the top of such floor
“the number of storeys contained between the roof and the floor
“the space between the roof and the ceiling of the top storey or
between a dwarf wall and a sloping roof.”
Drawn: a two-storey house on a basement, cut through to show six of the defined words. The first floor sits 900 mm above grade, so it is the first storey.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.2.1.1. (page 9-8), with definitions from Division A 1.4.1.2.
